newsitem.title: FRANCE: New U.N. approval for French wheat to Iraq.
newsitem.headline: New U.N. approval for French wheat to Iraq.

text.p: The United Nations has this week authorised a recent contract for the sale of 25,000 tonnes of French wheat to Iraq -- bringing to 325,000 tonnes the amount of French wheat approved for shipment under a U.N. oil-for-food pact, a French government source said on Friday.
Traders have in total sold 600,000 tonnes to 700,000 tonnes of French wheat for distribution to Iraqis since December when Iraq began exporting oil under the plan to relieve sanctions.
Under the plan's terms each contract must be approved by U.N. authorities in New York before deliveries can be made.
The U.N. sanctions panel therefore has another 275,000 to 375,000 tonnes of French wheat sales to sift through.
"It takes quite a long time. They have to examine the commercial contracts and then there are political considerations," the French source said.
Iraq complained last month to the United Nations about the length of time it was taking to deliver the food, though grain and other supplies have now started arriving at its borders.
A U.N. official in Iraq said on Thursday that over 400,000 tonnes of wheat bought under the oil-for-food plan would be inside the country by mid-April.
